- **self**: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime) (11/4)

## How it works

- [statement] Percona explains why redundancy matters during node maintenance: a two-voter replica set loses majority when one member stops; three members can maintain majority while one restarts. This is general replica-set guidance, not an Atlas resizing procedure. (low confidence) — https://www.percona.com/blog/tactics-to-scale-down-your-mongodb-deployment/ · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime)

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] One unresolved January 2024 report says an Atlas reduction from 32 GB to 8 GB was rejected after deletion and compact: the UI reported roughly 16.04 GB currently used despite the user's 6.15 GB data-usage reading. This establishes a reported eligibility problem, not its cause or present prevalence. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/unable-to-scale-down-atlas-clusters-storage-after-deleting-documents-and-running-compact/262189 · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime)

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Percona's maintenance guidance warns that removing a node can break majority availability in a two-voter replica set. This supports checking failover assumptions before maintenance; it is general MongoDB guidance rather than an Atlas topology recommendation. (low confidence) — https://www.percona.com/blog/tactics-to-scale-down-your-mongodb-deployment/ · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime)

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas documents capacity reduction as provisioning new volumes and synchronizing existing data into them; each affected node has downtime during the sync. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime) · also: https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-atlas-resize-clusters/view, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/scale-down-cluster-storage-with-no-downtime/312168
- [statement] The documented reduction workflow can retain cluster access while the node being modified remains unavailable until its data sync finishes. Large-cluster per-node syncs can take several hours; this is not a guaranteed duration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime)
- [statement] A February 2025 forum correction reports reducing storage directly through the Atlas UI and quotes support describing rolling changes beginning with secondaries, contradicting the thread's initial migration-only answer. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-11) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/scale-down-cluster-storage-with-no-downtime/312168 · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime)
- [statement] Treat storage reduction as maintenance that depends on replication and failover. PointFive recommends maintenance planning for the Atlas sync operation; Percona independently explains that MongoDB maintenance commonly relies on replica-set failover. Percona's guidance does not verify Atlas's internal orchestration. (medium confidence) — https://www.pointfive.co/efficiency-hub/inefficiencies/overprovisioned-mongodb-atlas-storage-after-auto-scaling · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime) · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/tactics-to-scale-down-your-mongodb-deployment/
- [statement] Node downtime does not necessarily mean cluster downtime: the documented rolling reduction leaves the cluster accessible while the modified node remains unavailable until synchronization completes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime) · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/scale-down-cluster-storage-with-no-downtime/312168
- [statement] Atlas warns that synchronization can take several hours per node on large clusters; this is a possibility, not a fixed maintenance-duration estimate. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/customize-storage.md · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime)
- [statement] OneUptime recommends checking driver retryReads/retryWrites and connection-pool limits before resizing, then polling cluster state until IDLE. These are operational checks; they do not establish that every application request survives a storage reduction. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-31) — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-atlas-resize-clusters/view · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime)
- [statement] PointFive recommends treating storage reduction as planned maintenance and sizing the target for data, indexes, and headroom. Its description of Atlas volume synchronization cites vendor documentation and is not an independent experimental confirmation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.pointfive.co/efficiency-hub/inefficiencies/overprovisioned-mongodb-atlas-storage-after-auto-scaling · keywords: Reducing Atlas storage capacity (new-volume sync, per-node downtime)
